title: Review: Momentum and its conservation; Impulse and force–time graphs
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: D09-ap2#t2 term and clue written for the game; D09-ap2#t3 term and clue written for the game; D09-ap1#t2 term and clue written for the game; D09-ap1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D09-ap1#N.6, D09-ap2#N.5, D10-1#N.12, D09-ap1#N.10, D09-ap2#N.10, D10-1#N.4b, D09-ap1#N.2, D09-ap1#N.8. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Component
items.clue: The x or y part into which a vector is split.

items.label: Elastic collision
items.clue: The only kind of impact in which kinetic energy is conserved.

items.label: Environment
items.clue: Where momentum flows to or from when the net external force is not zero.

items.label: Impulse
items.clue: Change in momentum that a third-law pair delivers equally and oppositely to A and B.

questions.stem: A cart of mass m moves with speed v along a level track toward a wall. It hits the wall and rebounds along the same line with speed v/3. Taking the cart's initial direction of motion as positive and the cart as the system, which expression gives the momentum transferred to the system from its surroundings during the collision?

An object of mass 4m at rest on a frictionless horizontal surface explodes into three pieces that slide along the surface. Immediately after the explosion, a piece of mass m moves at speed v in the +x-direction and a piece of mass 2m moves at speed 2v in the +y-direction. What is the speed of the third piece, of mass m?

Two identical 0.50 kg gliders on an air track each move at 2.0 m s⁻¹ towards an obstacle. Glider 1 hits a steel buffer and bounces straight back at 2.0 m s⁻¹; the contact lasts 0.010 s. Glider 2 hits a foam pad and stops; the contact lasts 0.040 s. How many times larger is the average force on glider 1 than the average force on glider 2?

options.text: 1, as both gliders arrive with the same speed

questions.stem: A box slides across a level floor and comes to rest because of friction. Which statement about the box's momentum is correct?

options.text: It was transferred to the Earth by friction, so the box–Earth total did not change.
It was destroyed by friction, which turned it into thermal energy in the box and floor.
It was not conserved, since momentum is conserved only in collisions and explosions.
It was transferred to the Earth, which gained the speed that the box lost.

questions.stem: An open cart of mass 3m rolls at speed v₀ along a level track with negligible friction. A ball of mass m falls vertically into the cart and stays in it; just before it lands, the ball's speed is 4v₀. What is the speed of the cart, with the ball in it, just after the ball lands?

Pucks A and B are at rest on level ice with negligible friction. Puck A has mass m, and puck B has mass 2m. Each puck is pushed by the same constant horizontal force F for the same time interval Δt. After the push, puck A has momentum of magnitude p_A. What is the magnitude of puck B's momentum after the push?
Two carts move along a straight track. Cart 1, of mass 3.0 kg, moves at +2.0 m/s, and cart 2, of mass 2.0 kg, moves at −1.0 m/s. What is the total momentum of the two-cart system?

Cart 1 rolls along a level track toward an identical cart 2, which is at rest. After they collide, cart 1 is at rest and cart 2 moves off with cart 1's original velocity. A student says that the collision cannot be elastic, because cart 1's kinetic energy changed. Which response to the student is correct?

options.text: Only the total kinetic energy of the two carts must be unchanged, and it is.
The student is right: in an elastic collision each cart keeps its kinetic energy.
Every collision conserves kinetic energy, since total energy is conserved.
The total momentum is unchanged, and that shows kinetic energy is too.
